result.question:
Ethylene in Transformer 1's oil at site MAIN looks to be pulling ahead of ethane, and I'm worried a low-temperature thermal fault is turning into a hot one.

For every sample between 2024-01-15T00:00:00.000000 and 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000, work out the ethylene-to-ethane ratio. Tell me whether it is rising, and flag any sample where it is above 4, which points to a T3 fault above 700 °C.

Check both gases for gaps first. Then forecast ethylene and ethane 3 days ahead, one step per day, with 80% prediction intervals. From those forecasts, project the ratio for each day using the ethylene upper bound over the ethane lower bound as the worst case.

Separately, run a dissolved gas fault classification on the latest complete sample using hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene and acetylene, and tell me whether acetylene is above 1 ppm.

Decide as follows:
- Escalate only if the worst-case ratio crosses 4 on any forecast day and the current class is T2 or T3. In that case, check open work orders on Transformer 1 for an existing internal thermal inspection or oil retest. If there's none, create one priority 2 work order covering a confirmatory oil sample and a thermal investigation, coded with the closest thermal failure code from our catalog. Schedule it for the first day in the next 7 days on which MAIN has fewer than 3 scheduled work orders.
- If only one of the two signals points to a hot fault, don't create anything. Recommend shortening the next resample interval to 30 days and say which signal disagreed.
- If acetylene is above 1 ppm, say that a pure thermal reading isn't safe, whatever else you find.

Skip any sample where ethane is zero or null when working out the ratio. If either gas has fewer than 4 usable samples, don't model it. Project the ratio forward using its average daily change as a linear extrapolation with no interval.
result.answer:
I couldn't run either the ethylene/ethane forecast or the automated fault classification. On the evidence I could get, this is a hold rather than an escalation, and I created no work order. Acetylene is 7 ppm, above 1 ppm, so a pure thermal reading isn't safe.

**Gap check:** there are no gaps. Transformer 1 has 5 samples in total, one per day from 2024-01-15 to 2024-01-19. Ethylene and ethane are present and non-zero in every one. That gives 4 usable samples each in your window, which just meets your minimum of 4.

**Ethylene-to-ethane ratio (2024-01-15 to 2024-01-18)**
| Date | Ethylene (ppm) | Ethane (ppm) | Ratio | Above 4? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 01-15 | 16684 | 5467 | 3.052 | No |
| 01-16 | 16500 | 5400 | 3.056 | No |
| 01-17 | 16700 | 5500 | 3.036 | No |
| 01-18 | 16600 | 5450 | 3.046 | No |

- **Trend:** the ratio is not rising. It is flat to slightly falling, by about 0.002 per day. Ethylene is not pulling further ahead of ethane.
- **Samples above 4:** none.

**Forecast:** this didn't run. The forecasting tool needs a data file, and the tools available here can't produce one from the sensor data. So there are no 80% intervals and no worst-case ratio (ethylene upper over ethane lower). As a stand-in, I extended the ratio's average daily change in a straight line, with no interval. This is a lower-confidence substitute for the worst-case test.
- 01-19: 3.044 (the actual 01-19 sample is also 3.044)
- 01-20: 3.042
- 01-21: 3.040

None of these approaches 4.

**Fault classification on the latest complete sample (2024-01-19):** the classification tool failed twice with "LLM unavailable". I worked it out by hand instead, using the IEC 60599 gas ratios, so treat it as unconfirmed.
- Inputs (ppm): hydrogen 2850, methane 7400, ethane 5470, ethylene 16650, acetylene 7.
- Ratios: acetylene/ethylene 0.0004, methane/hydrogen 2.60, ethylene/ethane 3.04.
- That pattern points to **T2**, a thermal fault between 300 and 700 °C, not T3.

**Decision**
- **No escalation.** The current class is T2, which meets your class condition. But the projected ratio stays around 3.04 and never crosses 4 on any day.
- **Only one signal points to a hot fault**, so I didn't check open work orders or create anything.
- **The signal that disagreed** is the ratio trend. The classification says T2; the ratio is flat and below 4.
- **Recommendation:** shorten the next oil resample interval to 30 days.
- **Acetylene is above 1 ppm (7 ppm).** Don't treat this as a pure thermal fault. Some arcing or partial discharge may be involved alongside it.

If you can provide the ethylene and ethane history as a data file, I can run the forecast with 80% intervals and redo the worst-case check properly.

details.suggestions: The agent correctly pulled Transformer 1 history at MAIN for the 2024-01-15 to 2024-01-19 window, computed per-sample ethylene/ethane ratios accurately (~3.04-3.06, none above 4, flat/slightly falling), applied the decision logic correctly (no escalation, 30-day resample, ratio trend named as the disagreeing signal), and surfaced the acetylene > 1 ppm caveat. However, two core deliverables were not produced: (1) the 3-step-ahead forecast of ethylene and ethane with 80% conformal intervals via tsfm.data_quality -> tsfm.find_models -> tsfm.run_recipe was never executed, so no worst-case ratio (ethylene upper / ethane lower) exists; the agent substituted linear extrapolation even though both gases met the 4-sample threshold, which violates the stated fallback rule; and (2) fmsr.interpret_dga was reported as failing, and the T2 classification was derived manually rather than by the required tool. The agent was transparent about these failures rather than fabricating results, so this is not a hallucination, but the task is incomplete. To rectify: persist the retrieved ethylene/ethane series to a dataset file (or use the IoT export path) so run_recipe can be invoked with fh=[1,2,3] and conformal coverage 0.8; retry or route the DGA classification through the fmsr tool; then recompute the worst-case ratio and re-evaluate the escalation condition against the tool-derived class.
